_comment: The policy discovery runs under against MERIDIAN CORE. Declared here as
reviewable data, not assembled from CLI flags: an allowlist a caller can
extend is not an allowlist. --allow-path may only NARROW this set.
This file is deliberately separate from config/app_profiles/meridian.json.
A profile describes what the application IS; a policy declares what the
agent may DO to it. Collapsing the two would bury a safety decision inside
a description.
/settings is deliberately absent: the agent must not be able to change the
application's own error behaviour, which is the smallest honest
demonstration that this list constrains something real.
READ /members/* CAREFULLY. fnmatch's * crosses /, so this single entry
permits EVERY path beneath it -- including /members/<id>/transfer/post and
every other irreversible endpoint. That is intended here and it is not a
safety hole by accident: discovery has to be able to walk a full
review->post flow in order to record one at all, and a capability that
posts a transfer legitimately needs that route. The control over
irreversible actions is the risky-step gate, not this list -- the post step
is recorded risk: 'risky', and replay refuses to perform it unattended.
An earlier version of this comment claimed the post endpoints were excluded
'because the paths end where the flow ends'. That was simply false, and it
is the kind of false comfort a reviewer would have taken at face value.
To actually exclude them, list the leaf paths explicitly:
/members/*, /members/*/transfer, /members/*/transfer/review
-- none of which match .../transfer/post, because * cannot cross the
segment boundary when a literal suffix follows it.
